messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty triggered: redwood-inference-canary — priority: P1 — reason: canary healthcheck failure (5/5 failures) — incident: INC-20250318-4123 — https://pagerduty.example/INC-20250318-4123
PagerDuty: Alert: redwood-inference-canary - CPU/latency anomaly during canary rollout. Paging: @Dev Oncall (primary) then @Alice Chen.
Dev Oncall: acked — I got the page, grabbing context.
Alice Chen: I’m on it, joining call now. Can someone paste canary deploy id?
Matt Rivera: deploy id = rollout/2025-03-18-canary-7f2a. Started 1758000000. Canary traffic = 5%.
Sara Patel: seeing spikes in tail latency and 502/503s from the canary group. Quick curl from k8s sidecar:

```
$ kubectl exec -it svc/inference-canary-7f2a -- curl -s -w "%{http_code}\n" -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
503
503
503
```

Matt Rivera: stack traces show inference runtime OOMs on a subset of variants. Logs from pod inference-canary-7f2a-2:

```
E 03:02:14 model_server.cpp:1422] kv cache alloc failed: out of memory
E 03:02:14 inference_loop.cc:291] runtime exception: CUDA out of memory
```

Alice Chen: interesting — only the canary variant (quantized-int8) is failing under traffic. Non-canary fleet is fine. Likely regression in the new quantization path/kernel selection.
Eng SRE Bot: Canary rollout automation: auto-rollout-check failed threshold=error_rate>2% over 3m. Initiating alert.
Dev Oncall: ETA for mitigation? Can we scale replicas to soak?
Sara Patel: scaling doesn't help if kernels OOM. We should stop traffic to the canary and revert to previous revision.
Matt Rivera: Agreed. Initiating immediate rollback to rollout/2025-03-08-stable-b2.

```
# rollback command
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deploy/inference-service --to-revision=20250308-b2
```

Dev Oncall: rollback issued at 1758001350. Watching pod churn.
Alice Chen: Confirmed new pods coming up with stable image. Healthchecks are green for stable.
Sara Patel: Canary group now receiving 0%. Traffic routing reverted. Telemetry: error-rate dropping to baseline.
PagerDuty: INC-20250318-4123 acknowledged by Dev Oncall (1758001289). Escalation canceled.
Eng SRE Bot: Running post-rollback checks: perf baselines, kv cache metrics, GPU memory alloc patterns.
Matt Rivera: Post-rollback logs show no OOMs. Example:

```
I 03:10:02 model_server.cpp:999] kv cache hit rate=0.92
I 03:10:02 inference_loop.cc:110] iteration complete, latency p95=42ms
```

Alice Chen: Starting short follow-up run: re-run the failing quantized variants under a non-production cluster to reproduce. Will file an internal bug if we can repro.
Dev Oncall: Handoff in 30m to @Sara Patel for monitoring and root cause follow-up.
Sara Patel: taking handoff. I’ll open INC-20250318 follow-up doc and assign to mgmt/infra.
Alice Chen: quick notes for postmortem:
- cause: regression in quantized-int8 kernel selection that increases transient memory usage under certain request shapes
- mitigation: immediate rollback, block the canary image until fix
- action items: add mem/alloc fuzz tests in CI, add hard OOM guard in canary policy, improve internal canary observability for kv cache misses

Matt Rivera: Customer impact: minimal — < 10% of internal canaries hit, no stable fleet impact; no customer-facing downtime. Notify support to watch for any customer reports.
Dev Oncall: Support pinged via #support with summary.
PagerDuty: Incident INC-20250318-4123 resolved: status = mitigated, resolution = rolled back canary image (1758001490).
Alice Chen: marking thread resolved. Will draft a short postmortem and link it here once ready.
Sara Patel: follow-up doc created: https://docs.internal/infra/incidents/INC-20250318-canary-quant-kernel. Assigning to @Matt Rivera for RCA.
Eng SRE Bot: Reminder: schedule follow-up review in 3 business days.
Dev Oncall: handoff complete to @Sara Patel at 1758001800. All clear from oncall side. :white_check_mark:
Alice Chen: thanks everyone — nice quick rollback.
PagerDuty: Note: if any new alerts from the same service occur, escalate to the Release Eng lead.
